recall_prompt: Say how you would do this one — say what a² is here, and which part of the expression the chain rule is applied to.

page_header: Section A — Very Short Answer Question

steps.label: Take the constant out and open the chain rule
steps.margin_note: First mark. a² holds no x, so it is a constant multiplier and comes straight outside. The mark is for writing d/dx(eˣ²) as eˣ² times the derivative of x², not for the arithmetic.
steps.memory_tip: Read a²eˣ² from the outside in: constant first, exponential next, x² innermost. Differentiate in that same order.
lines: Here a is a constant, so a² is a constant multiplier and stays outside.
For eᵘ the chain rule gives d/dx(eᵘ) = eᵘ · du/dx, and here u = x²

recall.must_convey: That a² is a constant taken outside, and that d/dx(eˣ²) = eˣ² times the derivative of x².
accept: a squared is a constant so take it outside
e power x squared differentiates to e power x squared times the derivative of x squared
use the chain rule with u equal to x squared
a square constant, bayata teesi rasi, tarvata chain rule
constant stays, then differentiate the exponential

steps.why: The letter a carries no x, so differentiating it would be treating a constant as a variable. Pulling a² out first leaves one clean chain rule to do, and that chain rule is the only real work in the question.
common_mistakes: Treating a² as a variable and differentiating it to 2a.
Writing d/dx(eˣ²) = eˣ² and stopping, with no inner derivative.

steps.label: Differentiate the inner x² and finish
steps.margin_note: Second mark. The factor 2x is the whole content of this mark. Without it the answer reads a²eˣ². The 2x is the first thing an examiner looks for.
steps.memory_tip: The 2 in the final 2a²x comes from the power 2 in x², not from the a².

recall.must_convey: That the inner derivative is 2x, giving 2a²x eˣ².
accept: the derivative of x squared is two x so the answer is two a squared x e power x squared
multiply by two x at the end
two a square x into e power x square
chivarlo two x tho multiply cheyyali
the inner derivative gives the two x factor

steps.why: The chain rule is only finished when the inner derivative is written. A missing 2x is the single most common way this two-line question loses a mark.
common_mistakes: Writing 2ax instead of 2a²x by dropping one power of a.

insider_note: a is a constant, so a² sits outside untouched — only eˣ² is differentiated. The chain rule on x² supplies the 2x that appears in the answer.
